rules.rationale: Source halide effect on refractive index was negative; by Moss relation low polarizability implies wide experimental gaps.
Chalcogenides carried the largest positive source refractive-index effect, which maps to small, polarizable-lattice band gaps.
Halogen-dominated ionic solids have deep p valence bands and high-lying cation states, giving very wide gaps.
Metalloid networks showed the strongest positive source index effect; covalent Si/Ge/Sb phases are typically narrow-gap.

skills.hypothesis: Refractive index and band gap are inversely coupled (Moss relation), so source effect signs should be flipped: halide/halogen chemistry gains weight, chalcogenide/metalloid loses it. Fails if heavy iodides or defect-rich halides dominate the pool.

rules.rationale: Oxide O 2p valence bands sit deep, producing large ionic bonding-antibonding separation in most experimental oxides.
Absence of partially filled d bands removes mid-gap states that collapse measured gaps in transition-metal compounds.
Low mean Z implies short, strong bonds and small spin-orbit effects, both widening experimental gaps.
Very heavy lattices are highly polarizable with strong spin-orbit splitting, systematically narrowing gaps.

skills.hypothesis: Domain proposal: wide experimental gaps come from light, closed-shell ionic chemistry without d-band states. May fail for wide-gap d0 oxides such as titanates that carry transition metals.

state.lesson: Source refractive-index effects likely transfer with inverted sign to band gap; the prior generation's sign-preserving chalcogenide/metalloid skill hovered near the anchor baseline on development seeds.
state.revision_summary: Replaced the sign-preserving transfer skill with a Moss-relation inverted version (halide/halogen up, chalcogenide/metalloid down) and added a domain skill favoring light, closed-shell, non-transition-metal ionic chemistry; deployed the inverted-transfer skill.
